scenes.tts: Adrenaline still fills this receptor, but the cell's response has faded. How can an occupied receptor lose its voice?
scenes.caption: Adrenaline still fills this receptor, but the cell's response has faded. How can an occupied receptor lose its voice?
scenes.visual: Hook on a dark field. A large membrane spans the frame. A yellow agonist remains locked in a yellow receptor. Green G proteins dock rapidly, then their departures slow sharply, but not to zero, while the agonist stays put. A large question mark grows beside the receptor. Label all cartoons 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Adrenaline still fills this receptor, but the cell's response has faded. How can an occupied receptor lose its voice?

scenes.visual: The carried membrane and receptor dim but remain visible. Title writes over them: The Mark and the Reader. Keep subtle membrane motion.

scenes.tts: Start with the receptor while it is active. Its inner face can meet a G protein and start another round of signaling. A dedicated receptor kinase then approaches that active shape. The kinase is called a G protein coupled receptor kinase, or G R K.
scenes.caption: Start with the receptor while it is active. Its inner face can meet a G protein and start another round of signaling. A dedicated receptor kinase then approaches that active shape. The kinase is called a G-protein-coupled receptor kinase, or GRK.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto the receptor's cytoplasmic face. A green G-protein block docks and leaves carrying an ON badge. A teal block labelled GRK follows the same route and settles beside the active yellow receptor. No molecular structure.
scenes.narration: Start with the receptor while it is active. Its inner face can meet a G protein and start another round of signaling. A dedicated receptor kinase then approaches that active shape. The kinase is called a G-protein-coupled receptor kinase, or GRK.

scenes.tts: The kinase adds phosphate marks to the receptor's cytoplasmic side. But a mark is not the same as an off switch. That distinction emerged when researchers purified the kinase and rebuilt signaling from isolated parts.
scenes.caption: The kinase adds phosphate marks to the receptor's cytoplasmic side. But a mark is not the same as an off switch. That distinction emerged when researchers purified the kinase and rebuilt signaling from isolated parts.
scenes.visual: Gold phosphate badges appear one at a time on the receptor tail. Transform the membrane into a large reconstitution tray containing labelled receptor, G protein, kinase and ATP blocks. A gauge reads 'G-protein activation'.
scenes.narration: The kinase adds phosphate marks to the receptor's cytoplasmic side. But a mark is not the same as an off switch. That distinction emerged when researchers purified the kinase and rebuilt signaling from isolated parts.

scenes.tts: Rebuilding the pathway made each requirement testable. The receptor sat in a lipid vesicle beside purified G protein. Researchers added candidate proteins one at a time. Receptor coupling became the readout, not phosphate alone.
scenes.caption: Rebuilding the pathway made each requirement testable. The receptor sat in a lipid vesicle beside purified G protein. Researchers added candidate proteins one at a time. Receptor coupling became the readout, not phosphate alone.
scenes.visual: Enlarge the reconstitution tray to fill the frame. Place a labelled receptor in a simple membrane vesicle, then add green G protein and teal kinase blocks separately. Animate the coupling gauge responding while the phosphate gauge remains a distinct readout.
scenes.narration: Rebuilding the pathway made each requirement testable. The receptor sat in a lipid vesicle beside purified G protein. Researchers added candidate proteins one at a time. Receptor coupling became the readout, not phosphate alone.

scenes.tts: A partly purified preparation added phosphate and strongly reduced receptor coupling. A highly purified kinase added phosphate too, yet coupling fell only a little. The phosphate signal remained. Most of the functional effect vanished.
scenes.caption: A partly purified preparation added phosphate and strongly reduced receptor coupling. A highly purified kinase added phosphate too, yet coupling fell only a little. The phosphate signal remained. Most of the functional effect vanished.
scenes.visual: Split the tray into two large panels. Left: 'partly purified', gold-mark gauge high, coupling gauge falls strongly. Right: 'highly purified', the same high gold-mark gauge, coupling gauge falls slightly. Values are qualitative and labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A partly purified preparation added phosphate and strongly reduced receptor coupling. A highly purified kinase added phosphate too, yet coupling fell only a little. The phosphate signal remained. Most of the functional effect vanished.

scenes.tts: The writer survived purification, but switching off did not. What missing part would make the phosphate mark matter?
scenes.caption: The writer survived purification, but switching off did not. What missing part would make the phosphate mark matter?
scenes.visual: Bring the two trays together. Highlight equal phosphate badges and unequal coupling gauges. Place an empty red outline labelled 'missing part?' between kinase and receptor. All other objects drift slowly.
scenes.narration: The writer survived purification, but switching off did not. What missing part would make the phosphate mark matter?

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction question. The empty red outline pulses gently while the marked receptor and active coupling gauge remain visible.

scenes.tts: A clue came from the retina. Its light receptor used a second protein, later called arrestin. Adding retinal arrestin to the rebuilt system brought back part of the lost effect. Arrestin alone could not act on an unmarked receptor.
scenes.caption: A clue came from the retina. Its light receptor used a second protein, later called arrestin. Adding retinal arrestin to the rebuilt system brought back part of the lost effect. Arrestin alone could not act on an unmarked receptor.
scenes.visual: The empty outline fills as a red block labelled arrestin enters from a small eye icon. It ignores an unmarked receptor. On the marked receptor, it closes around the cytoplasmic core like a clamp. The coupling gauge drops.
scenes.narration: A clue came from the retina. Its light receptor used a second protein, later called arrestin. Adding retinal arrestin to the rebuilt system brought back part of the lost effect. Arrestin alone could not act on an unmarked receptor.

scenes.tts: The controls narrowed the claim. An unrelated protein could not replace arrestin. Heat damaged arrestin could not replace it either. The effect required an intact reader and a receptor carrying the kinase's mark.
scenes.caption: The controls narrowed the claim. An unrelated protein could not replace arrestin. Heat-damaged arrestin could not replace it either. The effect required an intact reader and a receptor carrying the kinase's mark.
scenes.visual: Run three carried test lanes. An unrelated grey block bounces away; a faded heat-damaged red block collapses; intact red arrestin clamps only the gold-marked receptor. Finish with two highlighted requirements: intact reader and marked receptor.
scenes.narration: The controls narrowed the claim. An unrelated protein could not replace arrestin. Heat-damaged arrestin could not replace it either. The effect required an intact reader and a receptor carrying the kinase's mark.

scenes.tts: Now the two jobs separate cleanly. G R K writes the mark on the active receptor. Arrestin reads that mark and covers the surface needed by the G protein. The writer identifies the target. The reader produces the block.
scenes.caption: Now the two jobs separate cleanly. GRK writes the mark on the active receptor. Arrestin reads that mark and covers the surface needed by the G protein. The writer identifies the target. The reader produces the block.
scenes.visual: Return to one full-frame receptor. Animate a two-step ledger beside it: WRITER, teal GRK adds gold mark; READER, red arrestin clamps over the green docking outline. A green G protein approaches, cannot overlap the occupied core, and turns away.
scenes.narration: Now the two jobs separate cleanly. GRK writes the mark on the active receptor. Arrestin reads that mark and covers the surface needed by the G protein. The writer identifies the target. The reader produces the block.

scenes.tts: This is one layer of a larger rule. During a G protein coupled receptor response, each active layer fades when removal outruns production. Here, new receptor signaling stops because the mark and reader together prevent new G protein activation.
scenes.caption: This is one layer of a larger rule. During a GPCR response, each active layer fades when removal outruns production. Here, new receptor signaling stops because the mark and reader together prevent new G-protein activation.
scenes.visual: Keep the blocked receptor large. Above it, a balance bar labelled 'new activation' versus 'removal' tips toward removal. Below, the stream of departing green ON blocks dwindles. Label the balance 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: This is one layer of a larger rule. During a GPCR response, each active layer fades when removal outruns production. Here, new receptor signaling stops because the mark and reader together prevent new G-protein activation.

scenes.tts: Notice what the mechanism does not require. The agonist need not leave first. The receptor can remain occupied while its access changes. Desensitization therefore records regulation inside the cell, not simply disappearance of the outside signal.
scenes.caption: Notice what the mechanism does not require. The agonist need not leave first. The receptor can remain occupied while its access changes. Desensitization therefore records regulation inside the cell, not simply disappearance of the outside signal.
scenes.visual: Hold the yellow agonist firmly inside the receptor. A label 'agonist still bound' stays fixed while red arrestin blocks the green docking outline. Fade the outside-signal meter only slightly, but drive the G-protein activation stream down sharply, not to zero.
scenes.narration: Notice what the mechanism does not require. The agonist need not leave first. The receptor can remain occupied while its access changes. Desensitization therefore records regulation inside the cell, not simply disappearance of the outside signal.

scenes.tts: The receptor is not the whole pathway. Active G proteins, second messengers, and phosphorylated targets can persist after receptor coupling falls. Their removal processes decide how long the rest of the response lasts.
scenes.caption: The receptor is not the whole pathway. Active G proteins, second messengers, and phosphorylated targets can persist after receptor coupling falls. Their removal processes decide how long the rest of the response lasts.
scenes.visual: Pull back from the blocked receptor. Extend a carried chain downward: green active G protein, blue messenger pool, target with gold phosphate badge. Arrestin remains on the receptor while the downstream icons continue moving.
scenes.narration: The receptor is not the whole pathway. Active G proteins, second messengers, and phosphorylated targets can persist after receptor coupling falls. Their removal processes decide how long the rest of the response lasts.

scenes.visual: End card shows one centered line only: 'A GRK mark does little until arrestin reads it.' No subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
